In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Barium abundance in the Galactic disk presents a bimodal distribution, with a step at corotation.
the Barium abundance in the Galactic disk presents a bimodal distribution as a function of the Galactic radius.
, beyond corotation, the Barium abundance in the Galactic disk is bimodal, with a high metallicity branch and a low metallicity one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Barium abundance in the Cepheid stars is a function of their birth place.
the Barium abundance in the external disk, in general, is higher than in the inner disk.
the Barium abundance in the external Galactic disk is bimodal.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Barium abundance gradient of Cepheid stars is consistent with the scenario in which the thin disk of the Milky Way was formed in two distinct regions separated by a barrier at the corotation resonance.
, in the outer disk, the stars that are seen beyond corotation, and that have the lowest metallicity, have a Barium abundance that is lower than the average for the whole disk.
Barium is a good tracer of the chemical evolution of our Galaxy.
